submitted.rationale: All three measurements are at noise level (about ±2e-4 % EQE). That fits Sb–Y oxides being wide-gap materials (about 2.7–3.6 eV) under 2.1 eV light. Index 14 (Sb 0.236, in the Y3SbO7 region) is the only one with a positive EQE, 8.3e-5 %, so it is the best measured candidate.

rejected.reason: EQE -1.7e-4 %, noise level; Sb-rich, wide gap (Y3Sb5O12 HSE ~3.4 eV)
EQE -2.1e-4 %, noise level; MEGNet's near-zero gap for Y2Sb2O7 turned out to be an artifact

consultations.verdict: Support (weak): Y3Sb5O12 (Sb 0.625) is on hull per MACE with HSE gap ~3.4 eV; the Sb-rich end contains mixed-valence Sb phases likely to give the most sub-gap absorption at 2.1 eV, while Y-rich phases (Y3SbO7, 3.6 eV) are wider-gap. Tiny MEGNet gaps for YSbO3/Y2Sb2O7 are implausible and discounted.

Uninformative-to-weak support: Y3SbO7 (Sb 0.25) PBE gap 2.66 eV, still above 2.1 eV, but Sb-rich end gave ~0 EQE so sampling the Y3SbO7-region composition (index 14, Sb 0.236) explores the other side of the line.

Weak support: MEGNet predicts a near-zero gap for Y2Sb2O7 (mp-1345216). That is probably an artifact, but if it is even partly right, the Sb~0.5 region is the only place with absorption below 2.1 eV. Both ends of the line have been sampled and are at noise level, so index 22 (Sb 0.484) tests the midpoint.
